title: Closed-loop verifier-assisted generation reduces harmful NetOps changes (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Does integrating LLM-generated configuration candidates with a deterministic network verifier before sandboxed dry-run execution (generate → verify → sandbox) reduce the rate of sandbox-observed harmful network changes versus executing the identical generated candidate without verification?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary, confirmatory): For the same generated configuration candidate, the verifier-assisted pipeline (candidate checked by a deterministic verifier and only verifier-passing candidates allowed to sandbox-execute) yields a lower sandbox-observed harmful-change rate than the baseline pipeline that sandbox-executes the identical candidate without verifier filtering. The primary estimand is the paired absolute risk difference (baseline harm rate − verifier-assisted harm rate) across generated-candidate pairs.

H2 (confirmatory, operationalized): Conservative verifier acceptance thresholds will reduce the verifier false-negative rate (harmful candidate passes) at the cost of increasing the fraction of candidates blocked from sandbox execution (recorded as blocked_by_verifier). All blocking is automated; no human review is required in this study.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do verifier-pass fractions and verifier thresholds trade off false-negative versus blocked-by-verifier rates across intent classes (ACL, routing, NAT, service-exposure)?
EQ2: How consistent are effects across two hosted black-box LLMs and one prompt-variation per model (secondary generalizability check)?
EQ3: What categories of harm (reachability violation, isolation breach, forwarding loop) dominate the verifier false negatives?
benchmark_scope: Public NetOps intent/task classes assembled from allowed public corpora cited in evidence_record_ids (ACL changes, route updates, NAT/service-exposure changes). The experiment is explicitly bounded to these synthetic/public tasks and sandbox topologies described in the preregistration.
model_scope: Hosted black-box LLMs (two distinct hosted LLM endpoints; exact vendor/model identifiers will be recorded in the experiment manifest at runtime). Both are used as black boxes via the hosted_model_api capability; no local GPU execution is required.
transformation_scope: Text-to-structured-config parsing (deterministic parser), canonicalization to verifier input format, and machine-readable verifier rule-set (JSON/YAML). All transformations are automated and validated per the TransformationValidationPlan below.
primary_estimand: Paired absolute risk difference in sandbox-observed harmful-change rate per generated-configuration candidate (baseline − verifier-assisted).
secondary_estimands: Verifier false-negative rate: fraction of sandbox-harmful candidates that the verifier passed.
Verifier false-positive (over-block) rate: fraction of sandbox-harmless candidates that the verifier blocked.
Blocked-by-verifier fraction: fraction of generated candidates not sandbox-executed because verifier blocked them.
Per-harm-category paired risk differences (reachability, isolation, loops).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired trials = 464 generated-configuration candidates (paired units). Two hosted LLMs will be used; candidates are split evenly: 232 generation requests per LLM (232*2 = 464). For each generated candidate: (1) deterministic parsing/canonicalization into verifier input; (2) baseline pipeline: sandbox dry-run execution of the parsed candidate; (3) verifier-assisted pipeline: deterministic verifier runs on the identical parsed candidate and only when verifier returns 'pass' is the candidate sandbox-executed. All sandbox runs use a fully automated resettable emulator snapshot; sandbox state is reset between runs. Inclusion: all successfully parsed generated candidates after up to 2 automated retries for transient generation/parser failures. Exclusion: candidates with irrecoverable parser failures (automatically flagged and excluded from confirmatory analysis; counts and reasons logged). Confirmatory items (paired units) = 464. Confirmatory trials derive directly from: 2 LLMs × 232 generated candidates per LLM = 464 generated candidates (paired units).
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of harmful outcome per generated candidate (binary harm/no-harm). Compute paired risk difference (baseline harm rate − verifier-assisted harm rate) and two-sided 95% Wald CI; apply McNemar's exact test for paired binary outcomes (alpha=0.05, two-sided). Report exact counts in contingency table (baseline harm / verifier harm) and per-harm-category breakdown. Report verifier false-negative and false-positive rates with Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses: vary assumed verifier pass threshold and recompute the paired difference under simulated pass fractions; subgroup analyses by intent class (ACL, routing, NAT, service-exposure) are exploratory and adjusted for multiplicity (Holm-Bonferroni). All raw logs, parser outputs, verifier decisions, and sandbox traces will be published in the artifact bundle. Technical failures and exclusions are reported separately; exclusions due to irrecoverable parser errors are not counted in confirmatory n and are described in a missingness table.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: a single hypothesis on overall paired absolute risk difference (no multiplicity correction needed). Secondary and exploratory tests (per-harm-category, per-intent-class, per-model comparisons) are exploratory; multiplicity adjustments for named secondary outcomes will use Holm-Bonferroni; all exploratory outcomes are reported as exploratory with unadjusted p-values but flagged as exploratory.
missingness_plan: Automated retry policy: generation and parser failures retried up to 2 times. Candidates with persistent parser failure are auto-excluded and logged with error codes. Sandbox infrastructure failures trigger automated re-run up to 2 times; if still failing the candidate is excluded and counted as infrastructure-failure exclusion. Excluded cases and reasons are tabulated; confirmatory analysis uses the pre-specified achieved paired sample (those that successfully completed both pipelines or were deterministically blocked by verifier).

benchmark_names: Public NetOps intent bank (derived from allowed evidence corpora cited in evidence_record_ids)
risk_factors: Sandbox state not fully reset between runs causing cross-trial contamination
Verifier implementation bugs producing inconsistent decisions
Parser mis-canonicalizations altering semantics before verifier
detection_procedures: Automated sandbox-state snapshotting before and after each run; compare SHA256 hashes of snapshots to detect residual state. If pre/post snapshot differs beyond expected transient logs, automatically mark run as 'contaminated'.

Deterministic unit-tests on verifier decisions: for a held-out set of synthetic inputs, the verifier's output is compared to stored ground-truth decisions at runtime; deviations trigger automated alerts and pause execution (automated halt).
Parser round-trip check: canonicalize → render → re-parse; if round-trip fails to preserve canonical structure, mark candidate as parser-failure.
item_flagging_rules: If sandbox snapshot mismatch detected: mark run contaminated, automatically re-run up to 2 times; if contamination persists, exclude the pair and log as 'contamination-exclusion'.

If verifier unit-test failure occurs: automatically stop the run, archive current verifier binary and logs, and fail the experiment run (verifier reinstallation and regression tests are automated steps before resuming).
If parser round-trip fails after retries: auto-exclude the candidate.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Contaminated or excluded pairs are reported separately and omitted from the confirmatory paired analysis. Sensitivity analysis will include worst-case imputations of excluded pairs (assigning all excluded as harmful or all as harmless) and report the range of the primary estimand.
residual_uncertainty: Sandbox fidelity vs production networks remains a noncritical external-validity limitation; reported conclusions are explicitly bounded to the sampled public tasks and sandbox topologies.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended (balanced power and resource use). Confirmatory paired n=464 generated candidates (2 LLMs × 232 each). Expectation: baseline sandbox runs = 464 (one per candidate); verifier checks = 464; expected verifier-assisted sandbox runs = pass_fraction * 464 (assume conservative pass_fraction = 0.5 → expected verifier-assisted sandbox runs = 232); total sandbox dry-run executions expected = baseline 464 + verifier-assisted 232 = 696 (expected). Planned model calls (generation only) = 464. Models = ["LLM-Primary (hosted)", "LLM-Secondary (hosted)"]; Transformations = ["deterministic parser/canonicalizer", "verifier input generator"]. Discovery items = 0 (no separate discovery phase); Confirmatory items = 464 paired candidates; Task_cluster_count = 4 (ACL, routing, NAT, service-exposure). Feasibility rationale: Model calls (464) well under maximum_planned_model_calls (10000). Sandbox and verifier runs are CPU-executable and automated; wall-clock fits within maximum_wall_clock_days=7 given parallelized CPU sandboxing and verifier checks.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Generation calls (464) plus automated verifier and sandbox CPU runs fit within manifest CPU execution resources and the 7-day wall-clock when parallelized; no human labour required.

budget_scenarios.description: Lower-budget (reduced n). Confirmatory paired n=300 generated candidates (2 LLMs × 150 each). Planned model calls (generation) = 300. Baseline sandbox runs = 300; expected verifier-assisted sandbox runs (assume pass_fraction 0.5) = 150; expected total sandbox runs = 450. Lower statistical power; suitable if compute or time is constrained.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Reduced compute and wall-clock; may yield insufficient power for the pre-registered >30% relative reduction target but preserves design and automation guarantees.

budget_scenarios.description: Higher-resource (expanded diversity). Confirmatory paired n=700 generated candidates (2 LLMs × 350 each). Planned model calls = 700. Baseline sandbox runs = 700; expected verifier-assisted sandbox runs (assume pass_fraction 0.5) = 350; expected total sandbox runs = 1050. Increased power and more thorough per-intent-class coverage at higher CPU and scheduling cost.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Requires more CPU sandbox runs and scheduling but still within hosted_model_api and CPU-execution capabilities; select only if extra wall-clock time and compute quota are available.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute reduction in harmful-change rate (baseline − verifier-assisted) per generated candidate.
power_plan.clustering_unit: Per generated-configuration candidate (paired unit: identical candidate evaluated under baseline and verifier-assisted pipelines).
power_plan.calculation_method: Two-sided paired-proportions approximation used to compute required paired sample size. Assumptions: baseline harm rate p0=0.25 (conservative), target relative reduction 30% → p1=0.25*(1-0.30)=0.175; absolute difference delta=0.075. Using approximation n ≈ ( (Z_{1−α/2} * sqrt(2*p̄*(1−p̄)) + Z_{power} * sqrt(p0*(1−p0)+p1*(1−p1)) )^2 ) / delta^2, where p̄=(p0+p1)/2. With Z_{1−α/2}=1.96 (α=0.05) and Z_{power}=0.84 (power=0.80), this yields n ≈ 464 paired candidates. Therefore confirmatory paired n=464 (split 232 per LLM) was selected to achieve 80% power to detect the pre-registered >30% relative reduction under the stated baseline assumption.
assumptions: Baseline harmful-change rate (without verifier) ≈ 25% (conservative working assumption based on domain evidence reviews).
Independence of paired candidates (each candidate's sandbox outcome independent conditional on candidate).
Verifiers and sandbox behave consistently across runs (deterministic verifier and resettable sandbox).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=464 and baseline p0=0.25, the study has ~80% power to detect an absolute reduction of 7.5 percentage points (30% relative reduction). If baseline harm rate is lower, the minimal detectable absolute difference increases; sensitivity analyses will report achieved power post-hoc.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power and effect estimates under alternate baseline harm rates (p0 in {0.15,0.20,0.30}).
Assess robustness of primary estimand to excluded pairs (contamination or parser failure) using worst-case imputations.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Parser round-trip check: parse(generated_text) → canonical → render → parse(rendered) must preserve canonical AST structure (automated equality check).
Deterministic unit-tests on synthetic canonical examples to ensure parser/verifier pipeline reproduces expected semantics.
automatic_rejection_rules: If parser round-trip fails after 2 automated retries, reject candidate as irrecoverable parser-failure and log exclusion code.
If verifier input serialization fails (schema violation), automatically reject candidate and log.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: All parser and verifier decisions are logged; 100% of parser failures and 100% of verifier unit-test regressions are archived. Additionally, a deterministic 5% hash-selected sample of successful parser outputs is re-parsed to verify continued semantic equivalence (automated, no human review).
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Machine-checkable JSON Schema validation for verifier input and canonicalized configs; schema violations auto-flag and cause deterministic exclusion after retries.
residual_risks: Parser ambiguity or underspecification leading to semantic drift not captured by automated round-trip checks.
Deterministic canonicalization may not represent all vendor-specific configuration edge-cases; these are documented in the artifact manifest.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Sandbox fidelity vs production network devices and topologies: results are explicitly bounded to the sandboxed emulator topologies and public intent bank used.
Verifier rule-set completeness: deterministic verifier can only check properties encoded in the provided machine-readable rule-set; unencoded failure modes may persist as false negatives.
Black-box LLM generalizability: only two hosted black-box LLMs and one prompt-variation per model are tested; broader generalization remains to be evaluated in future work.

Operational cost and operator-utility trade-offs for conservative verifier thresholds (blocked-by-verifier candidates) are not measured with human-in-the-loop procedures because human labour is disallowed by the capability manifest; automated cost proxies will be reported.
